rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> two-year (2009, 2010) split-plot field experiment at CCRI Multan with drip vs furrow main plots and seven weed-control sub-plots, three replications. Q2: Results, 'Weed density' section and Table 1 <U+2013> all drip-irrigated treatments showed a significant 19-24% decrease in total weed density at 60 DAS compared with furrow irrigation (77.9 vs 102.7 m-2 in 2009; 87.5 vs 108.4 m-2 in 2010); weed dry matter also lower under drip (69.9 vs 101.3; 84.7 vs 114.0 g m-2).
rows.notes: Q3: weed density and weed dry matter come from the same quadrat sampling of the same plots <U+2013> one method. Q4: the mechanism (lower soil-moisture availability to weeds under drip) is asserted and attributed to Choudhary et al. 2012; soil moisture was not measured. Q5: single site, single crop (cotton CIM-557), two seasons. Q6: 7 m x 3 m plots only. Q7: no condition stated as a requirement for the effect. Q8: no limitations stated. Q9: only LSD values and letter groupings are given; no SD/SE/CI for the weed-density means <U+2013> treated as 'no' with some doubt since LSD is derived from the standard error of the difference. The 19-24% figure is a range across years, not a dispersion measure.

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and Methods <U+2013> own two-year split-plot field experiment (drip vs furrow, cotton, Multan, Pakistan). Q2: Results and Table 1 <U+2013> drip irrigation significantly reduced weed density (19-24%) and weed dry matter at 60 DAS relative to furrow irrigation in both 2009 and 2010; Discussion restates that drip significantly suppressed weed population and dry-matter accumulation.
rows.notes: Same study result supports this claim (reduction in weed growth under drip vs furrow in cotton). Q3: single measurement method (quadrat counts/weights). Q4: soil-moisture mechanism only asserted, citing other work. Q5: one site, one crop. Q6: plot scale only. Q7: no requirements stated from own findings. Q8: no limitations given. Q9: LSD and letter groupings only; no SD/SE/CI for the irrigation effect on weeds.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a two-season field trial at one site in Multan, Pakistan; drip vs furrow irrigation effects on weeds are confounded with no separate soil-moisture measurement. Note the weed-density reduction under drip is reported as a main effect across all weed-management sub-plots, consistent with the claims.
